headline: Gusty, wet front tonight into Sunday, then a drier spell midweek.
summary: Pacific storms are pushing through western Washington, with a dip in the high-altitude winds, called an upper-level trough, over the area and a stronger front following. Tonight into Sunday brings steady rain and gusty south winds, strongest on the coast and San Juan Islands, plus a Wind Advisory there. A flood watch covers the Skokomish River. Sunday brings showers and easing winds. Monday stays unsettled, mainly in the hills, and turns cooler. A deep low is expected near the coast Wednesday, but most of its rain should stay south of the region. A drier spell follows Thursday, though forecasters are unsure about the midweek low and what comes next weekend, when wetter weather could return.
changes: Earlier discussions expected the midweek storm track to stay well south of the region, with a dry, cool outlook. The latest discussion describes a deep low approaching the coast Wednesday, with less certainty about how close it gets.
